name: Cinema Studio Video
summary: Cinema Studio in motion: the same film look as the still, then up to three camera moves, a tempo and sound, on LTX-2.5.

source.notes: Higgsfield's Cinema Studio 4.0 has an image and a video mode with the same film settings (genre, era, tempo), camera (body, lens, aperture and 33 camera moves, several per shot in order), palette and lighting, read on 26 Oct. Here the video mode is the LTX-2.5 image-to-video template whose first frame is drawn in the same graph by cinema-studio's still (FLUX 3 Image Klein, nodes still:*): the look selects write the still's prompt, which Klein follows closely, and the motion prompt adds the camera moves in order, the tempo and the action. Camera move names from Higgsfield's list; each option writes the movement it describes.

inputs.label: Scene
inputs.default: A detective in a trench coat lights a cigarette under a streetlamp on a rainy night, then looks up as headlights sweep across his face
inputs.help: What happens in the shot. The first frame is drawn from it with the look below, then the shot moves.

bind.template: A cinematic film still{genre}{era}: {prompt}. The look: {camera}; {lens}; {focal}; {aperture}. Lighting: {lighting}. Color: {palette}. High dynamic range, ultra-detailed
{moves}{prompt}.{tempo} The look of a film{genre}{era}: {camera}; {lens}. Lighting: {lighting}. Color: {palette}.

inputs.label: Camera move
default: slowly dollies in toward the subject
inputs.help: Up to 3, in order: the shot does them one after the other.

inputs.help: The editing rhythm. Single shot keeps one take; Dynamic and Chaotic ask for cuts.
